messages.text:
PowerShell by name has the same spawn issue, so I’m using the absolute executable path for npm scripts.

This is a small environment wrinkle, but the project itself is staying standard: `npm install`, `npm run build`, and the scripts remain normal for the user.

commands.commandLine: "C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe" -Command '$root=(Resolve-Path .).Path; $nm=(Join-Path $root '"'node_modules'); "'$pl=(Join-Path $root '"'package-lock.json'); if((Test-Path "'$nm) -and ((Resolve-Path $nm).Path.StartsWith($root))){ Remove-Item -LiteralPath $nm -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; if(Test-Path $pl){ Remove-Item -LiteralPath $pl -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; npm install --script-shell "C:'"\\WINDOWS\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe\""
